a_restatement: Memory in AI agents is a described architecture rather than a marketing claim—models identify and extract valuable information from interactions and store it as timestamped memory objects.

When queried, the system retrieves relevant memories by comparing query embeddings to stored memory embeddings using similarity measures like cosine distance, keeps a top-ranked subset, and orders results by timestamp.
Users can delete memories explicitly or schedule deletion for later, and the memory system shapes both what agents communicate and what actions they take through potential API calls.

b_answers.answer: The model decides what to store based on predictions of what is worth remembering, extracting from cached inputs that go to the model system.
b_answers.quoted_span: A model decides what to store: cached inputs go to the model system, which predicts what is worth remembering and extracts it.

b_answers.answer: The stored information ends up as a memory value within a memory object.
b_answers.quoted_span: It is stored as a memory value in a memory object

b_answers.answer: The agent ranks stored objects by relevance using query embeddings compared to memory value embeddings through cosine similarity or similar measures, keeps a top subset, and orders them by timestamp.
b_answers.quoted_span: At query time the agent does not reread everything; it ranks stored objects by relevance to your query. It compares a query embedding to memory value embeddings by a measure such as cosine similarity, keeps a top subset, and orders them by timestamp.

b_answers.answer: The system deletes the specified information.
The system queues the information for deletion, and objects past their expiration time are deleted during maintenance.
b_answers.quoted_span: "forget this after three months" queues it for deletion. Objects past their expiration time are deleted during maintenance

b_answers.answer: The old memory object is replaced or updated with the new information, and aligned objects can be consolidated into one; contradictions refine the memory rather than overcorrecting it.
b_answers.quoted_span: new timestamped input is matched to the prior memory object it concerns, which is then replaced or updated. Aligned objects can be consolidated into one, and a contradiction refines the matched memory rather than overcorrecting it.

b_answers.answer: Memoryless agents force users to re-enter the same details repeatedly. This system differs through a described architecture with structured memory objects made from interactions, retrieved by relevance, corrected over time, and deleted when requested—not merely a slogan.
b_answers.quoted_span: Agents forget, so you re-enter the same details; the claim is a loop — query plus memory data from a datastore of your past interactions, into a sequence model, out as a response. ... What is claimed is structural: memory objects made from your interactions, some on your explicit request, retrieved by relevance, corrected over time, and deleted when you ask. That is a described architecture, not a slogan.
